scope: All verified named simulator platforms in the benchmark catalog, plus four explicitly used robot-learning frameworks. Not an exhaustive catalog of robotics simulation software.

simulators.name: MuJoCo
simulators.description: Articulated dynamics and contact for manipulation, locomotion and model-based control.
simulators.note: General-purpose articulated models; concrete assets, actuators and task definitions come from environment packages. MJX and MuJoCo Warp provide related acceleration paths. Open-sourced May 2022; the milestone here is the original 2012 paper.

paper.title: MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Introduction; articulated structures, contact, model formats and project history.
Curated robot models include arms, hands, humanoids and quadrupeds.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

benchmarks.name: ManiSkill family
benchmarks.note: ManiSkill is powered by SAPIEN. Versions differ in parallelization and supported tasks.

benchmarks.name: RoboMME
benchmarks.note: RoboMME uses a ManiSkill-based SAPIEN environment.

sources.locator: ManiSkill acknowledgement and SAPIEN renderer configuration

benchmarks.name: MIKASA-Robo / MIKASA-Robo-VLA
benchmarks.note: MIKASA-Robo and its VLA edition use ManiSkill environments on SAPIEN.

benchmarks.name: RoboMME-Interference
benchmarks.note: The interference protocol directly uses RoboMME tasks and its environment.

benchmarks.name: FailBench: VLM success judging
benchmarks.note: This is an offline video-judging benchmark, not a live simulator. Its simulated source clips come from Meta-World / LIBERO (MuJoCo) and SimplerEnv (SAPIEN); it also includes real videos.

benchmarks.name: SIMPLER
benchmarks.note: SIMPLER uses SAPIEN through ManiSkill2; a ManiSkill3 branch offers GPU-parallel environments.

simulators.name: OmniGibson
simulators.description: Household scenes and tasks with object state changes, materials, navigation and manipulation.
simulators.note: Built on Isaac Sim for the BEHAVIOR ecosystem. Supports rigid/deformable objects, fluids and task predicates. The selected BEHAVIOR-1K paper covers the simulator together with the benchmark.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: BEHAVIOR-1K: A Human-Centered, Embodied AI Benchmark with 1, 000 Everyday Activities and Realistic Simulation
paper.note: Counts the BEHAVIOR-1K paper, not an OmniGibson-only paper or all BEHAVIOR editions.

github.scope: BEHAVIOR-1K monorepo, which includes OmniGibson and other ecosystem components.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

benchmarks.name: BEHAVIOR-1K and BEHAVIOR challenges
benchmarks.note: BEHAVIOR-1K uses OmniGibson, which is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Omniverse.
